     5	/// Bounded restart policy for an app-managed engine. The schedule is indexed
     6	/// from one, and stays at its final value when callers allow more attempts
     7	/// than explicit delays. Keeping this policy separate from process launching
     8	/// makes the operational limits straightforward to test and tune.
     9	struct EngineRestartPolicy: Equatable, Sendable {
    10	    static let `default` = EngineRestartPolicy(
    11	        backoffSchedule: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30],
    12	        maximumAttempts: 6,
    13	        pollInterval: 1,
    14	        healthyResetInterval: 60,
    15	        consecutiveFailureThreshold: 3
    16	    )
    17	
    18	    let backoffSchedule: [TimeInterval]
    19	    let maximumAttempts: Int
    20	    let pollInterval: TimeInterval
    21	    let healthyResetInterval: TimeInterval
    22	    let consecutiveFailureThreshold: Int
    23	
    24	    init(
    25	        backoffSchedule: [TimeInterval],
    26	        maximumAttempts: Int,
    27	        pollInterval: TimeInterval = Self.default.pollInterval,
    28	        healthyResetInterval: TimeInterval = Self.default.healthyResetInterval,
    29	        consecutiveFailureThreshold: Int = Self.default.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    30	    ) {
    31	        self.backoffSchedule = backoffSchedule.isEmpty ? Self.default.backoffSchedule : backoffSchedule
    32	        self.maximumAttempts = max(1, maximumAttempts)
    33	        self.pollInterval = max(0.1, pollInterval)
    34	        self.healthyResetInterval = max(0, healthyResetInterval)
    35	        self.consecutiveFailureThreshold = max(1, consecutiveFailureThreshold)
    36	    }
    37	
    38	    func delay(forAttempt attempt: Int) -> TimeInterval {
    39	        backoffSchedule[min(max(0, attempt - 1), backoffSchedule.count - 1)]
    40	    }
    41	
    42	    static func fromEnvironment(_ environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment) -> Self {
    43	        let schedule = environment["BOSS_ENGINE_RESTART_BACKOFF_SECONDS"]?
    44	            .split(separator: ",")
    45	            .compactMap { TimeInterval($0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)) }
    46	            .filter { $0 > 0 && $0.isFinite }
    47	        let attempts = environment["BOSS_ENGINE_RESTART_MAX_ATTEMPTS"].flatMap(Int.init)
    48	        return Self(
    49	            backoffSchedule: schedule ?? [],
    50	            maximumAttempts: attempts.map { max(1, $0) } ?? Self.default.maximumAttempts
    51	        )
    52	    }
    53	}

   143	    private func start(resetRestartBudget: Bool) throws {

   145	        try withStartLock {
   146	            if forceRestart, let running = discoverRunningEngine() {
   147	                emit("[engine restart] terminating existing engine \(describe(running))")

   149	            }
   150	
   151	            if let running = discoverRunningEngine() {
   152	                // An engine is already running. Check if its binary matches
   153	                // the app's bundled engine. If not, replace it so the user
   154	                // always gets the version that shipped with this app launch.
   155	                //

   157	                // "engine wasn't restarted after I updated Boss" can grep
   158	                // the system messages and tell exactly which path fired:
   159	                //   [engine version-check skipped: <reason>] — check didn't run
   160	                //   [engine version-check ok] — ran, fingerprints matched
   161	                //   [engine upgrade] — ran, fingerprints differed, restarting
   162	                //
   163	                // BOSS_ENGINE_CMD wins unconditionally (see
   164	                // resolveEngineCommand): a dev running against a custom
   165	                // engine binary has nothing bundled to compare it to, and
   166	                // fingerprinting the *bundled* binary against it would
   167	                // always mismatch and tear down the dev's own engine.
   168	                if ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["BOSS_ENGINE_CMD"] != nil {
   169	                    emit("[engine version-check skipped: BOSS_ENGINE_CMD is set (developer custom engine)] attaching to \(describe(running))")
   170	                    return
   171	                }
   172	                guard let bundledPath = bundledEnginePath() else {
   173	                    emit("[engine version-check skipped: no bundled engine in app resources (dev/bazel-run mode)] attaching to \(describe(running))")

   175	                }
   176	                guard let bundledFP = computeBinaryFingerprint(path: bundledPath) else {

   178	                }
   179	
   180	                // A single missed 3s deadline can mean "the engine is busy",
   181	                // not "the engine is stale" — retry a couple of times before
   182	                // treating non-response as a mismatch, so a slow-but-healthy
   183	                // engine isn't torn down and replaced (and doesn't then hit
   184	                // the SIGTERM/SIGKILL fallback if the follow-on shutdown RPC
   185	                // also times out).

   187	                var fingerprintAttempts = 0

   189	                while fingerprintAttempts < maxFingerprintAttempts {
   190	                    fingerprintAttempts += 1
   191	                    runningFP = socketControl.fingerprint(socketPath: running.socketPath, timeoutSeconds: 3.0)
   192	                    if runningFP != nil { break }
   193	                }

   195	                guard let runningFP else {
   196	                    emit("[engine version-check inconclusive] running fingerprint unavailable after \(fingerprintAttempts) attempts bundled=\(bundledFP) — keeping reachable \(describe(running))")

   198	                }

   200	                    emit("[engine version-check ok] running=\(runningFP) matches bundled — attaching to \(describe(running))")
   201	                    return
   202	                }
   203	                emit("[engine upgrade] running=\(runningFP) bundled=\(bundledFP) — replacing \(describe(running))")

   236	    /// Compute a binary fingerprint of `path` using the same algorithm
   237	    /// as `boss_engine::build_info::binary_fingerprint`:
   238	    ///   SHA-256 of up to 64 MiB of file content → first 6 bytes as
   239	    ///   12 lowercase hex digits, optionally suffixed "-truncated".
   240	    private func computeBinaryFingerprint(path: String) -> String? {
   241	        guard let fh = FileHandle(forReadingAtPath: path) else { return nil }
   242	        defer { try? fh.close() }
   243	
   244	        let cap: Int = 64 * 1024 * 1024
   245	        var hasher = SHA256()
   246	        var readTotal = 0
   247	        var truncated = false
   248	        let chunkSize = 64 * 1024
   249	
   250	        while true {
   251	            let remaining = cap - readTotal
   252	            guard remaining > 0 else {
   253	                // Probe for more bytes to set the truncated flag.
   254	                let probe = (try? fh.read(upToCount: 1)) ?? Data()
   255	                if !probe.isEmpty { truncated = true }
   256	                break
   257	            }
   258	            let toRead = min(chunkSize, remaining)
   259	            guard let chunk = try? fh.read(upToCount: toRead), !chunk.isEmpty else { break }
   260	            hasher.update(data: chunk)
   261	            readTotal += chunk.count
   262	            if chunk.count < toRead {
   263	                // EOF before cap.
   264	                break
   265	            }
   266	        }
   267	
   268	        let digest = hasher.finalize()
   269	        let firstSixBytes = digest.prefix(6)
   270	        let hex = firstSixBytes.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined()
   271	        return truncated ? "\(hex)-truncated" : hex
   272	    }

   393	    private func checkEngineLiveness() {
   394	        guard !isSupervisionStopped, pendingRestart == nil else { return }
   395	        let liveness: (isReachable: Bool, source: String)
   396	        if let livenessProbe {
   397	            liveness = (livenessProbe(), "engine client connection")
   398	        } else {
   399	            liveness = (discoverRunningEngine() != nil, "socket probe")
   400	        }
   401	        let action = supervisor.tick(isAlive: liveness.isReachable, now: Date())
   402	        switch action {
   403	        case .running:
   404	            lastLaunchError = nil
   405	            emitSupervisionState(.running)
   406	            return
   407	        case let .unreachable(consecutiveFailures, requiredFailures):
   408	            emit("[engine supervision] \(liveness.source) reported engine unreachable; failed liveness tick \(consecutiveFailures)/\(requiredFailures), keeping engine running")
   409	            return
   410	        case let .gaveUp(attempts):
   411	            emit("[engine supervision] gave up after \(attempts) restart attempts; use Restart engine to try again")
   412	            emitSupervisionState(.gaveUp(attempts: attempts, lastError: lastLaunchError))
   413	            return
   414	        case let .restart(attempt, delay):
   415	            emit("[engine supervision] engine remained unreachable for \(restartPolicy.consecutiveFailureThreshold) consecutive ticks; restart attempt \(attempt)/\(restartPolicy.maximumAttempts) in \(Int(delay))s")

   417	            let work = DispatchWorkItem { [weak self] in
   418	                self?.relaunchAfterUnexpectedExit(attempt: attempt)
   419	            }
   420	            pendingRestart = work
   421	            supervisionQueue.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + delay, execute: work)
   422	        case .wait:
   423	            return
   424	        }
   425	    }

   432	        } catch {
   433	            lastLaunchError = error.localizedDescription
   434	            emit("[engine supervision] restart launch failed: \(error.localizedDescription)")

   447	    private func launchDetached(command: String, bossBinDir: String?, socketPath: String) throws -> pid_t {
   448	        let launchErrorPath = URL(fileURLWithPath: paths.pidPath)
   449	            .deletingLastPathComponent()
   450	            .appendingPathComponent("engine-launch.log")
   451	            .path
   452	        let proc = Process()
   453	        proc.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/bin/zsh")
   454	        // zsh's BG_NICE option (on by default) reduces the priority of any
   455	        // job started with `&` by a non-interactive shell — nice(5) rather
   456	        // than the caller's own nice(0) — because a `zsh -c` script has no
   457	        // job control (monitor mode) active. That silently demoted the
   458	        // detached engine, and everything it forks (the private tmux
   459	        // server, then the coordinator's `claude` pane inside it) inherit
   460	        // that nice(5) by plain fork inheritance. `NO_BG_NICE` keeps the
   461	        // backgrounded engine at the same priority as this app.
   462	        //
   463	        // This only reaches a tmux server started by a post-fix engine: a
   464	        // private server already running under the durable state-root socket
   465	        // is never killed by this codebase, so on an existing install it
   466	        // keeps the nice(5) it was born with even after this fix ships. After
   467	        // upgrading, `tmux -S "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Boss/tmux.sock"
   468	        // kill-server` (or a reboot) once so the next engine launch creates a
   469	        // fresh server under this corrected priority. A leftover `-L boss`
   470	        // server is drained at boot rather than relocated.
   471	        let script = """
   472	        setopt NO_BG_NICE
   473	        : > \(shellQuote(launchErrorPath))
   474	        nohup \(command) >/dev/null 2>\(shellQuote(launchErrorPath)) &
   475	        child=$!
   476	        print -r -- $child
   477	        sleep 0.25
   478	        if ! kill -0 $child 2>/dev/null; then
   479	          wait $child
   480	          exit $?
   481	        fi
   482	        """
   483	        proc.arguments = ["-c", script]
   484	        proc.currentDirectoryURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: launchDirectory, isDirectory: true)
   485	        // Tell the engine the app's pid explicitly. `bazel run`
   486	        // daemonizes its server, which reparents the engine binary
   487	        // away from the app's process tree, so `getppid()` and any
   488	        // ancestor walk both miss the real app. The engine reads
   489	        // BOSS_APP_PID to set its trust root for `RegisterAppSession`.
   490	        var env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
   491	        env["BOSS_APP_PID"] = String(getpid())
   492	        // The engine's tracing layer continues writing its bounded text log,
   493	        // while direct startup failures from Rust's main function land in the
   494	        // launch-error file above for this controller to surface verbatim.
   495	        env["BOSS_ENGINE_STDERR_LOGGING"] = "0"
   496	        // BOSS_BIN_DIR tells the engine where its sibling CLIs live
   497	        // (boss, bossctl, boss-event) in installed mode. The engine
   498	        // propagates this to workers so they resolve the bundled copies
   499	        // rather than any PATH match. Unset in dev mode (no bundle bin/).
   500	        if let dir = bossBinDir {
   501	            env["BOSS_BIN_DIR"] = dir
   502	        }
   503	        // When launched from Finder/Dock/launchctl, the app inherits a minimal
   504	        // launchd GUI session PATH (/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin) that omits
   505	        // developer tool directories. The engine and its cube subprocesses need
   506	        // jj, mint, and other tools that live outside that minimal set.
   507	        //
   508	        // We prepend well-known locations rather than shelling out to read the
   509	        // user's login-shell PATH (which would be more accurate but brittle — a
   510	        // misbehaving shell init could hang the app or print garbage). Extra
   511	        // segments that don't exist on a given machine are ignored by the kernel.
   512	        env["PATH"] = augmentedPATH(current: env["PATH"] ?? "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin")

## Orientation

Boss should keep a working background service available instead of replacing it merely because a version check gets no answer. This bug fix changes the macOS app’s engine management: it preserves a reachable service when its version cannot be determined, still replaces a confirmed different build, and waits for repeated failed reachability checks before scheduling recovery.

The **engine** is the separate background process the app communicates with; it can survive an app restart. A **socket** is the local communication endpoint used to reach it. A **fingerprint** is an identifier calculated from the engine executable, used to compare the running build with the one bundled in the app. An **RPC** is a request sent to that separate process, such as asking for its fingerprint. **Supervision** is the app’s periodic reachability checking; each check is a **tick**.

## Change overview

Two decisions become less aggressive:

- At startup, three unsuccessful fingerprint requests previously led to stopping the reachable engine. They now produce an “inconclusive” message and retain it. A returned fingerprint that differs from the bundled fingerprint still triggers replacement.
- During supervision, one failed reachability tick previously scheduled recovery. The default now requires three consecutive failed ticks. Intermediate failures identify the signal source and failure count in diagnostic messages.

These are distinct checks: being reachable does not establish that the running build matches, and a failed reachability signal does not establish that the process exited. The changed [startup branch](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L205) and [supervision dispatch](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L393-L424) preserve that distinction.

## Core implementation

The existing division of responsibility stays intact. "'`EngineProcessController` performs discovery, version requests, process operations, and timer scheduling. `EngineSupervisor` is the decision-making state machine: it receives a reachability boolean and a time, then returns an action. `EngineRestartPolicy` supplies the limits and **backoff**, the delay before each recovery attempt.

The policy adds `consecutiveFailureThreshold`, defaulting to three and clamped to at least one. Existing defaults remain one-second polling, six recovery attempts, delays of 1/2/4/8/16/30 seconds, and a 60-second healthy interval for replenishing the attempt allowance. See [policy initialization](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L9-L39).

## Implementation walkthrough

### 1. Treat an unavailable fingerprint as an unknown version

Discovery first finds a reachable socket. The unchanged [socket helper](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/BossEnginePaths.swift#L256-L291) separates connecting successfully from obtaining a fingerprint: the latter can return `nil` when the request yields no usable response, the response type is wrong, or the fingerprint field is absent.

Startup retains its three fingerprint attempts, each with a three-second timeout argument. The decisive new branch is:

```swift
guard let runningFP else {
    emit("[engine version-check inconclusive] running fingerprint unavailable after '"\\(fingerprintAttempts) attempts bundled=\\(bundledFP) — keeping reachable \\(describe(running))\")
    return
}
"'```

In the [surrounding code](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L186-L219), this return exits the startup-lock closure, avoiding shutdown and launch; startup still proceeds to enable supervision unless supervision has been stopped. Matching fingerprints also return, while a nonmatching returned fingerprint reaches `stopRunningEngine`.

The existing [startup exceptions](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L143-L178) remain: forced restart acts before the version check, custom-engine configuration or an absent bundled engine skips comparison, and failure to fingerprint the bundled file throws an error.

### 2. Worked example: reachable service, unanswered version requests

The [new controller regression test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L224-L238) supplies a reachable primary socket, a bundled executable fixture, and a fake fingerprint service that returns `nil`.

1. Discovery succeeds, so startup enters version comparison.
2. All three fingerprint requests return `nil`.
3. **Before:** the [merge-base branch](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L182-L207) treated this as replacement evidence and called `stopRunningEngine`, then launched a replacement if stopping succeeded.
4. **After:** the new guard logs the inconclusive result and leaves the existing process alone. The test asserts exactly three fingerprint requests, no shutdown requests, and no launches.

The observable effect is that a missing version answer no longer causes the app to replace this reachable engine. The contrasting case remains explicit: the existing [stale-build test](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L209-L222) returns `"stale-engine"` from the legacy socket—the older supported endpoint—and asserts shutdown there followed by launch on the primary socket.

### 3. Require consecutive failures before spending a recovery attempt

Previously, the supervisor proceeded from a failed tick directly to [attempt accounting](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/6f8ca35153d0fcae9aea5e9852894ea549989ca0/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L43-L55). It now increments a failure counter and, while the recovery allowance is not exhausted, applies this gate:

```swift
guard consecutiveFailures >= policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold else {
    return .unreachable(
        consecutiveFailures: consecutiveFailures,
        requiredFailures: policy.consecutiveFailureThreshold
    )
}
consecutiveFailures = 0
```

The [full transition logic](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineSupervisor.swift#L25-L65) clears the streak on any healthy tick or explicit reset. Reaching the threshold clears the streak before accounting for an attempt, so later recovery attempts also require a new streak. Exhausted supervision still returns `.wait`; sustained health still restores the allowance.

The new test makes the default threshold concrete: failed ticks produce `.unreachable(1, 3)`, then `.unreachable(2, 3)`, then `.restart(attempt: 1, delay: 1)`. This is a count of checks, not a requirement that exactly three seconds elapse.

### 4. Connect the decision to scheduling and diagnostics

The app already [supplies its engine-client reachability signal](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/ChatViewModel.swift#L1215-L1226). The controller continues to use that signal when supplied, otherwise discovering a reachable socket. It now labels the source “engine client connection” or “socket probe.”

An intermediate `.unreachable` action only logs the source and failure count; it neither schedules recovery nor emits a new supervision state. At the threshold, the message describes consecutive unreachability instead of claiming “engine exited,” and the existing delayed recovery work is scheduled. Checks are skipped while that work is pending.

Crucially, recovery calls `start(resetRestartBudget: false)`, so it reuses discovery and the revised version decision rather than unconditionally killing a process. These behaviors are together in the [controller’s action handling and recovery callback](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/EngineProcessController.swift#L393-L435). Diagnostic output uses the existing [system-message callback](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/ChatViewModel.swift#L1275-L1281).

## Tests and supporting infrastructure

**Added tests:**

- [`testUnresponsiveReachableEngineIsKeptWithoutReplacement`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L224-L238) checks three unanswered fingerprint requests without shutdown or launch.
- [`testDebouncesSingleUnreachableTickBeforeSchedulingRestart`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift#L75-L90) checks two intermediate failure actions followed by recovery on the third consecutive failure.

**Modified tests:** Three existing supervisor tests explicitly set the threshold to one, preserving their focus on attempt exhaustion, restoration after 60 seconds of health, and immediate restoration after reset. Their [assertions remain focused on those behaviors](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/EngineRestartPolicyTests.swift#L32-L73). No tests are removed.

**Fixture changes:** [`FakeSocketControl`](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/68e51b6cfd5cb8ccac6473273d04d57fe972d7a4/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/BossCaptureTests.swift#L291-L329) now accepts an optional fingerprint. The fake returns immediately; the new test exercises unavailable responses rather than waiting through real network timeouts. No build or test-runner configuration changes are included.

- `checkleft run`

Boss should keep a working background service available instead of replacing it merely because a version check gets no answer. This bug fix changes the macOS app’s engine management: it preserves a reachable service when its version cannot be determined, still replaces a confirmed different build, and waits for repeated failed reachability checks before scheduling recovery.
